header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are often polysemantic, activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: neurons are often polysemantic, activating for several unrelated types of feature
Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits polysemantic neurons
Language models can explain neurons in language models
neuron explanations GPT-4 automated interpretability simulate activations
Bills neuron explainer language models explain neurons
neuron responds to cat faces and car fronts

args.quote: polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda
One natural question to ask is why do polysemantic neurons form?

events.delta:
Verdict: supported for the Olah et al. (2020) citation; the Bills et al. (2023) part cannot be checked because that paper is not in the library.

**The sentence.** It appears in the introduction of *Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models* (Cunningham et al.): "Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are often polysemantic, activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020)." (arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p1)

**Olah et al. (2020), supported.** The cited work is *Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits* (Distill), which is in the library. It supports the polysemanticity claim:
- It calls polysemantic neurons a problem: "polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda" (distill:zoom-in/r1/b65). This is somewhat stronger than the source's own word "often", so the paraphrase is reasonable.
- It gives an example of a neuron that does not respond to a shared feature: "this neuron isn't responding to some commonality of cars and cat faces. Feature visualization shows us that it's looking for the eyes and whiskers of a cat, for furry legs, and for shiny fronts of cars" (distill:zoom-in/r1/b64). This is the "several unrelated types of feature" point.
- It asks why such neurons form and links them to superposition: "One natural question to ask is why do polysemantic neurons form?" (distill:zoom-in/r1/b66).

**Bills et al. (2023), not verifiable.** *Language models can explain neurons in language models* is not in the library. Its only trace is the reference-list entry in arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p10. So I could not confirm the "some success" claim about using individual neurons as units. The Olah et al. support above covers only the polysemanticity clause.
